scope: AMD AIE API 2026.1 reference refresh and read-only FastFlowLM host binary analysis; no production runtime change

amd.retrieval: Downloaded with curl; browser tool could not open the URL. HTML and extracted text retained in ignored evidence directory.
observations: XDNA2 f16 x f16 matrix cell is empty; prior local compiler rejection remains consistent.
Float matrix multiplication is emulated using native BF16 multiplication (footnote d).
BF16 8x8x8 uses block-floating-point emulation enabled by AIE_API_EMULATE_BFLOAT16_MMUL_WITH_BFP16, with an accuracy tradeoff (footnote e).
Documentation version does not establish the installed headers/compiler version; new APIs require local compilation and numerical validation.

source_cross_checks: FastFlowLM/src/include/hrx_cpp/hrx_cpp.hpp: executable cache keyed by length-prefixed full xclbin and transaction bytes; record dispatches, start records then flushes, runlist records all then flushes once.
FastFlowLM/src/CMakeLists.txt: FLM_USE_HRX defaults OFF; HRX is opt-in.
limits: Analysis decodes x86 host instructions, not embedded AIE device instructions.
Multiple dispatches followed by one flush/wait do not prove one hardware command or a speedup.
GEMM getters alone do not establish native INT8 MAC execution.
Earlier XRT runlist ERT_CMD_STATE_ABORT does not establish HRX incompatibility.
HRX runtime compatibility and performance have not been measured in this project.
next_measurements: Check availability and ABI of the pinned HRX runtime; build a C++ control using identical existing artifacts and buffers.
Compare individual start/wait against record-many/flush/wait, including executable reuse, changing inputs, state order, guards and numerical equivalence.
Only integrate after serial hardware A/B measurements establish reduced host/dispatch cost without numerical or prefill regressions.

validation.performance: Not applicable to this documentation-only change; no HRX performance claim.
